entries.subject: PDS Voyager ISS original and calibrated products
entries.finding: The OPUS surface-geometry inventory contains 3,422 observations. The finest indexed product is vg-iss-2-u-c2675821, about 35.93 km/pixel, with a 5.76 s exposure and 5:1 scan mode. Portia spans only a few independent image samples. This supports the published size/elongation analysis, but not a useful resolved cartographic texture. Inventory and original metadata are pinned. No imagery is painted onto the model.
entries.revisitWhen: A Portia observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Karkoschka (2001) adopted Voyager/HST shape
entries.finding: Table IV of the HST study supplies the adopted prolate semiaxes 78 × 63 × 63 km. The repeated minor axis is a model assumption, not an independently measured third dimension. French et al. (2024), Table 3 reproduces the separate Voyager size paper’s projected-radius and axis-ratio uncertainties; they are not individual-axis errors. The selected analytic shape supplies no local relief or surface pixels.

entries.subject: 2023 Keck near-infrared study and HST photometry
entries.finding: Integrated brightness/reflectivity measurements, using adopted body sizes; they do not supply spatially resolved color pixels. Excluded as a surface color lens.
entries.revisitWhen: A spatially resolved Portia measurement supplies original spectral or image samples with body-fixed coordinates and enough coverage to qualify a mapped lens.

entries.subject: USGS/PDS mapped products, elevation, geology and spectroscopy
entries.finding: No registered Portia surface, elevation or compositional map was located in the relevant archive and cited-release survey. Integrated spectral measurements are distinct from a mapped surface dataset. This is a bounded survey result, not a claim that no other observations exist.
entries.revisitWhen: A spatially resolved Portia measurement supplies original spectral or image samples with body-fixed coordinates and enough coverage to qualify a mapped lens.
